pageProps.title: Defining Custom Image and Distro for Raspberry Pi Zero 2W
pageProps.review: Learn how to automate manual configurations and efficiently build and manage your own images by adding image recipes and distribution settings to a custom Yocto layer for the Raspberry Pi Zero 2W.
pageProps.description: A guide to creating custom image recipes and distribution configurations in your own Yocto layer, eliminating the need for manual local.conf edits
pageProps.content: ## Defining Custom Image and Distro for Raspberry Pi Zero 2W I'll complete the layer for creating my own image by adding an `image recipe` and `distribution configuration` to the meta-jooojub-rpi layer created in the previous post. I will now apply the modifications I previously made to `local.conf` and `bblayers.conf` for the Raspberry Pi Zero 2W image directly to the layer. This eliminates the need for manual edits, allowing you to create images immediately just by adding the layer, which simplifies maintenance and distribution. ### 1. Add Image recipes Previously, we used `core-image-base` when building images with bitbake. You can create custom image recipes based on this base image. Create files and directories in the following paths within the `meta-jooojub-rpi` layer created in the previous post. I've configured it to be buildable with the name jooojub-rpi0-2w. ```bitbake { "title": "recipes-core/images/jooojub-rpi0-2w.bb" } --- $ mkdir -p recipes-core/images $ vi recipes-core/images/jooojub-rpi0-2w.bb # Base this image on core-image-base include recipes-core/images/core-image-base.bb COMPATIBLE_MACHINE = "^rpi$" ``` Since `core-image-base` is included, you can now build the image using jooojub-rpi0-2w. ```bash $ bitbake jooojub-rpi0-2w ``` ### 2. Create Distro Configuration To minimize modifications to the existing `local.conf`, create your own Distro. ```shell { "title": "conf/distro/rpi0-2w.conf" } --- $ vi conf/distro/rpi0-2w.conf require conf/distro/poky.conf DISTRO = "rpi0-2w" DISTRO_NAME = "Jooojub Raspberry Pi zero 2W" DISTRO_VERSION = "1.0" LICENSE_FLAGS_ACCEPTED += "synaptics-killswitch" # 16GB rootfs space IMAGE_ROOTFS_EXTRA_SPACE = "16777216" ``` You can now add the LICENSE and `IMAGE_ROOTFS` size settings, which were previously modified in `local.conf`, here instead. ### 3. Create conf Templates When running `oe-init-build-env` to set up the initial build environment, you can specify your own templates. By default, poky/meta-poky/conf/templates is used. I'll make this part customizable as well to minimize additional tasks. Copy the templates from the existing `meta-poky`. ```shell { "title": "Copy default template" } --- $ cp -rf ../meta-poky/conf/templates conf/ ``` Now, add the desired parts. To avoid the hassle of manually adding layers every time, I've configured them to be included automatically during initial setup. ```diff { "title": "conf/templates/default/bblayers.conf.sample" } --- ##OEROOT##/meta \ ##OEROOT##/meta-poky \ ##OEROOT##/meta-yocto-bsp \ + ##OEROOT##/meta-raspberrypi \ + ##OEROOT##/meta-jooojub-rpi \ + ##OEROOT##/meta-openembedded/meta-oe \ + ##OEROOT##/meta-openembedded/meta-python \ + ##OEROOT##/meta-openembedded/meta-networking \ " ``` I've modified the message displayed by `oe-init-build-env` to include a list of buildable targets. ```diff { "title": "conf/templates/default/conf-notes.txt" } --- You can now run 'bitbake ' Common targets are: - core-image-minimal - core-image-full-cmdline - core-image-sato - core-image-weston - meta-toolchain - meta-ide-support + jooojub-rpi0-2w ``` Modify the MACHINE and DISTRO values that need to be added to `local.conf` to your preferred values. ```diff { "title": "conf/templates/default/local.conf.sample" } --- #MACHINE ?= "genericx86-64" # # This sets the default machine to be qemux86-64 if no other machine is selected: -MACHINE ??= "qemux86-64" +MACHINE = "raspberrypi0-2w-64" +DISTRO = "rpi0-2w" ``` ### 4. Build Test Let's check if the modifications made so far work correctly. I'll boldly delete the existing build directory and configure the build using my custom conf templates. Simply specify the path to the previously created templates in the `TEMPLATECONF` environment variable. Using an absolute path is recommended. ```shell { "title": "Create build env with TEMPLATECONF" } --- $ TEMPLATECONF=`pwd`/poky/meta-jooojub-rpi/conf/templates/default source poky/oe-init-build-env build ... You can now run 'bitbake ' Common targets are: jooojub-rpi0-2w ... ``` You can see that the modifications to `conf-notes.txt` are displayed correctly. ```bash { "title": "conf/bblayers.conf" } --- --- BBLAYERS ?= " \ /raspberrypi-zero2/poky/meta \ /raspberrypi-zero2/poky/meta-poky \ /raspberrypi-zero2/poky/meta-yocto-bsp \ /raspberrypi-zero2/poky/meta-raspberrypi \ /raspberrypi-zero2/poky/meta-jooojub-rpi \ /raspberrypi-zero2/poky/meta-openembedded/meta-oe \ /raspberrypi-zero2/poky/meta-openembedded/meta-python \ /raspberrypi-zero2/poky/meta-openembedded/meta-networking \ " ``` The layers are correctly added to `conf/bblayers.conf` as well. ```bash { "title": "conf/local.conf" } --- ... MACHINE = "raspberrypi0-2w-64" DISTRO = "rpi0-2w" ... ``` The desired `MACHINE` and `DISTRO` values are also present in `conf/local.conf`. Since the desired values are included by default, you can run bitbake immediately to generate the image. ```bash $ bitbake jooojub-rpi0-2w ``` ### 5. Next Steps The basic foundation for customizing Yocto recipes is now in place. I'll start adding the features I want one by one.
